# `Q-1-20` — Failed to parse metadata value as markdown

> Quarto tried to parse a metadata value as markdown and could
> not. The value will be treated as a plain string.

## What this means

Quarto 2 parses string-valued YAML metadata as markdown by default,
so that markup like `*emphasis*` and `[links](./other.qmd)` inside
fields such as `title:` or `subtitle:` renders correctly downstream.
This error fires when the markdown parser cannot make sense of the
value.

The error comes in two flavors:

- **Warning** when the value carries no explicit tag and the
  markdown parse fails: Quarto falls back to treating the value as
  a plain string and continues.
- **Error** when the value is explicitly tagged `!md` (forcing
  markdown interpretation) and the markdown parse fails: Quarto
  cannot honor the tag, so it rejects the value.

## Why this happens

Most often, a metadata string that looks ordinary contains
characters the markdown parser interprets as syntax:

- A value with unbalanced square brackets, parentheses, or
  asterisks looks like an incomplete link or emphasis run.
- A value beginning with `#` looks like a heading.
- Pipe characters or backticks can look like table or code syntax.

## How to fix

For values you want to keep as plain strings, add the `!str` tag:

```yaml
title: !str "Q-1-20: a markdown puzzle"
```

The `!str` tag tells Quarto to skip markdown parsing for this
value, so any of the characters above pass through unchanged.

For values you genuinely want to render as markdown, fix the
markdown so that it parses. The message includes the underlying
markdown parser's diagnostic — the same error the text would
produce in a document body, with spans pointing into your YAML
file — so it shows exactly which part of the value failed to
parse, and why.

If the value is explicitly tagged `!md` and you do not actually
need markdown interpretation, remove the tag.
